prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker for everyone — the right choice depends on your budget, ad style (live‑action, avatar, animated, text→video), output platform (TikTok, YouTube, Meta), need for scale/personalization, and how much creative control you want. Below are top options by use case plus quick pros/cons and what to look for when choosing.

Top picks (brief):

- Synthesia / HeyGen
  - Best for: fast, realistic AI presenters/avatars and multilingual narrator ads.
  - Pros: realistic talking avatars, many languages, fast turnaround, simple script→video.
  - Cons: avatars limit “live-action” variety; subscription cost for higher output.

- Pictory
  - Best for: turning long-form content or scripts into bite‑size social ads.
  - Pros: transcript-based editing, automatic captioning, stock footage, good for repurposing.
  - Cons: less control for full custom animation; template-driven.

- InVideo / Promo.com / VEED.ai
  - Best for: template-based social ads with lots of design/branding options.
  - Pros: big template libraries, drag‑and‑drop, stock clips, decent AI text-to-video features.
  - Cons: creative limits if you want bespoke visual effects.

- Runway
  - Best for: creative/generative video editing (background replacement, image → video).
  - Pros: advanced generative tools, strong editing features for unique ads.
  - Cons: steeper learning curve; best for teams with some video skills.

- Descript
  - Best for: editing spoken-word ads, overdub voice, captioning, multitrack editing.
  - Pros: word-based editing, clean audio tools, convenient for repurposing interviews/podcasts.
  - Cons: less emphasis on motion graphics/templates.

- Vyond
  - Best for: animated explainer ads and brand storytelling.
  - Pros: character-based animation, strong for explainer-style creatives.
  - Cons: animation look is stylized; less “realistic” video.

- Elai.io / Rephrase.ai
  - Best for: scaled personalized video (first-name personalization at scale).
  - Pros: automated personalized video generation for large campaigns.
  - Cons: pricey at scale; avatar limitations.

How to choose (checklist):
- Ad format: short vertical (TikTok/IG Reels) vs horizontal (YouTube) vs square.
- Speed vs control: templates = faster; custom editing = more control.
- Personalization: need to insert names/data at scale?
- Presenter type: human-like avatar, voiceover, or animated characters?
- Languages/voices: required languages and accents.
- Budget: free tier/low-cost vs enterprise subscriptions.
- Output quality & rights: HD export, commercial usage of stock assets.
- Trial and support: free trial, templates, customer service, performance tips.

Pricing (very rough):
- Low-cost/freemium: Pictory, Lumen5, InVideo (from ~$10–30/month for creators).
- Mid-tier: Synthesia, HeyGen, VEED, Descript (~$25–100/month).
- Enterprise/scale: Synthesia Studio, Runway, Elai enterprise tiers (custom pricing).

Recommendation by common use case:
- Social short ads with branding and quick turnaround: InVideo, Promo.com, VEED.ai.
- Corporate explainer or multilingual presenter ads: Synthesia or HeyGen.
- Repurposing webinars/podcasts into shorts: Pictory + Descript.
- High‑creativity or generative visuals: Runway.
- Scaled personalized campaigns (first name/video per user): Elai.io or Rephrase.ai.
- Animated product explainer: Vyond.

If you tell me: budget, platform (TikTok, Meta, YouTube), preferred style (real actor, avatar, animated, text + stock footage), and whether you need personalization or multi‑language support, I can recommend 2–3 specific tools and a sample workflow to produce an ad.
